You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 623fd246bb40234fe68dd4e7c1f1f081f9c45a3d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alexandre Kroupski <alexandre.kroupski@ingenico.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Aug 2019 08:37:45 -0300
Subject: [PATCH] media: atmel: atmel-isi: fix timeout value for stop streaming

In case of sensor malfunction, stop streaming timeout takes much longer
than expected. This is due to conversion of time to jiffies: milliseconds
multiplied with HZ (ticks/second) gives out a value of jiffies with 10^3
greater. We need to also divide by 10^3 to obtain the right jiffies value.
In other words FRAME_INTERVAL_MILLI_SEC must be in seconds in order to
multiply by HZ and get the right jiffies value to add to the current
jiffies for the timeout expire time.

Fixes: 195ebc43bf76 ("[media] V4L: at91: add Atmel Image Sensor Interface (ISI) support")
Signed-off-by: Alexandre Kroupski <alexandre.kroupski@ingenico.com>
Reviewed-by: Eugen Hristev <eugen.hristev@microchip.com>
Signed-off-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+samsung@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/media/platform/atmel/atmel-isi.c b/drivers/media/platform/atmel/atmel-isi.c
index d7d94c1a39d3..428f117caa59 100644
--- a/drivers/media/platform/atmel/atmel-isi.c
+++ b/drivers/media/platform/atmel/atmel-isi.c
@@ -493,7 +493,7 @@ static void stop_streaming(struct vb2_queue *vq)
 	spin_unlock_irq(&isi->irqlock);
 
 	if (!isi->enable_preview_path) {
-		timeout = jiffies + FRAME_INTERVAL_MILLI_SEC * HZ;
+		timeout = jiffies + (FRAME_INTERVAL_MILLI_SEC * HZ) / 1000;
 		/* Wait until the end of the current frame. */
 		while ((isi_readl(isi, ISI_STATUS) & ISI_CTRL_CDC) &&
 				time_before(jiffies, timeout))
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/media/platform/atmel/atmel-isi.c`**
   - The line calculating the `timeout` for stopping the streaming has been modified. 
   - The original line:
     ```c
     timeout = jiffies + FRAME_INTERVAL_MILLI_SEC * HZ;
     ```
   - Has been changed to:
     ```c
     timeout = jiffies + (FRAME_INTERVAL_MILLI_SEC * HZ) / 1000;
     ```
   - This change divides the product of `FRAME_INTERVAL_MILLI_SEC` and `HZ` by 1000 to correctly convert milliseconds to jiffies, addressing the issue of the timeout taking longer than expected in case of sensor malfunction.

### Relationships

- The modification in `atmel-isi.c` directly addresses a bug related to the timeout value for stopping streaming, which was incorrectly calculated due to a misunderstanding of the time conversion from milliseconds to jiffies. 
- The patch is linked to a previous commit (identified by the hash `195ebc43bf76`) that introduced the Atmel Image Sensor Interface (ISI) support, indicating that the bug fix is a correction to the functionality added in that earlier commit. 
- The patch has been reviewed and signed off by multiple individuals, suggesting that it has undergone scrutiny and validation before being applied.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
timeout = jiffies + FRAME_INTERVAL_MILLI_SEC * HZ;
```
Reason:
The timeout value for stopping streaming is calculated by multiplying `FRAME_INTERVAL_MILLI_SEC` (which is in milliseconds) by `HZ` (ticks per second). This results in a timeout value that is 1000 times longer than intended because the conversion from milliseconds to jiffies is not properly handled; it should have been divided by 1000 to obtain the correct jiffies value.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
timeout = jiffies + (FRAME_INTERVAL_MILLI_SEC * HZ) / 1000;
```
Reason:
The fix involves dividing the product of `FRAME_INTERVAL_MILLI_SEC` and `HZ` by 1000, which correctly converts the milliseconds to seconds before calculating the timeout in jiffies. This adjustment ensures that the timeout value is accurate, preventing unnecessary delays in stopping the streaming in case of sensor malfunction.
